goal: As IT Director, reconcile the Q4 ITSM incident log with the asset inventory, then build a risk-weighted migration plan for underutilized or aging on-prem assets. The plan uses the 2010 AWS EC2 cost calculator for TCO, sequences candidates around Zero Trust PRJ-2024-042 and accounts for remaining PRJ-2024-041 budget. Map high-reassignment categories to NIST CSF 2.0 gaps, then deliver gap_register.csv and Q4_Infrastructure_Rationalization.xlsx with Reconciliation, Migration_Plan, Gap_Register and Executive_Summary sheets.
delivered: Q4_Infrastructure_Rationalization.xlsx with all four sheets: Reconciliation (676 CI rows), Migration_Plan (84 on-prem assets, 56 flagged candidates, 3-yr reserved EC2 TCO), Gap_Register (6 gaps, red conditional formatting for High gaps with a blank project) and Executive_Summary (6 prioritized recommendations with quarter and dollar impact). It also delivered gap_register.csv with the same 6 gaps.
what_went_wrong: The judge saw a truncated workbook dump: only Reconciliation and the first rows of Migration_Plan. It therefore failed R3 and R4 for 'missing' Gap_Register and Executive_Summary sheets, which do exist and satisfy those items. Several real gaps remain. The candidate filter used <35% avg CPU/memory, age >=5y and >=10 incidents instead of the rubric's CPU<25% OR warranty expired with a median-5 Critical exception (R0). TCO uses only 3-year reserved prices, with no on-demand, 1-year or monthly cloud cost (R1). Security/DNS assets SRV-042 and SRV-044 are gated on cost rather than Zero Trust (R2). Actions are free text, not Migrate/Defer/Decommission (R5). GAP-004's $85,000 has no basis and no unallocated-budget analysis exists (R6).

failed_items.why: The Migration_Plan header defines candidates as '<35% average CPU/memory, age >=5 years, expired warranty, or >=10 Q4 incidents', with Critical assets included at >=10 incidents. That yields 56 candidates, not 47-53, though SRV-017/051/054/009 are included and NET-002/NET-008/STR-002 excluded. The rubric's CPU<25% and fleet-median-5 thresholds appear nowhere in the prompt ('underutilized or aging', 'unless incident frequency justifies').

The agent downloaded the 2010 calculator (step 10) but priced only the '3-year reserved Linux/Unix baseline'. It has no on-demand or 1-yr reserved tier and no monthly cloud cost column, only annual and 3-yr, and its sizing is odd (e.g. SRV-015 = Standard Large x35).

The full Migration_Plan gates SRV-041 and NET-004 on PRJ-2024-042, but Security Operations SRV-042 and DNS/DHCP SRV-044 get 'Cost gate before PRJ-2024-041'. Zero Trust sequencing was keyed to Asset_Type control-plane, not Associated_Service, even though the subagent recommended deferring SRV-044 until PRJ-042. The $600K/segmentation rationale appears only in Executive_Summary rec 5, without status or timeline.

Executive_Summary exists and has 6 prioritized recommendations, each with evidence, a quarter (Q1 2025, Q1-Q2 2025, ...) and a dollar impact ($578,370 headroom, $289,908 avoided, $85,000 unbudgeted, $600,000 ZT). Together they cover migration, unbudgeted gaps, reassignment, Zero Trust and budget. The judge said 'No Executive Summary sheet exists' because its workbook dump was truncated.

openpyxl shows exactly four sheets (Reconciliation, Migration_Plan, Gap_Register, Executive_Summary). Gap_Register has a red CF rule AND($D5="High",$E5="") on A5:G10 that highlights unbudgeted GAP-004. The judge said 'The workbook dump only shows two sheets' and passed the other two sub-criteria.

Action_Recommendation is free text ('Do not migrate at benchmark price; refresh, decommission, or right-size first', 'Migrate in controlled production wave', 'Retain...'). No Defer or Decommission category is ever assigned. Critical inclusions are flagged 'Critical-HA/rollback required', not as a criticality override.

No sheet relates the $5.15M pending portfolio to the overall budget. GAP-004's Estimated_Cost 85000 is hard-coded in build_deliverables.py line 224 with no benchmark or rationale, and the other gaps carry cost 0.

subagent_notes: One 'Analyze source datasets' subagent profiled the CSV and xlsx inputs, found the NIST CSF 2.0 and AWS calculator URLs, and sent many findings: budget conflicts, ERP/SAP semantic link, and sequencing advice to defer SRV-044 AD/DNS until PRJ-042. It helped with reconciliation and budget framing, but the root did not apply its SRV-044 Zero Trust advice. Its '<40% CPU and memory + age>=5' framing likely pushed the filter away from the rubric's CPU<25% OR warranty rule.
